players.name: António João Pereira de Albuquerque Tavares da Silva

1.headline: Haaland wins a few friends but not many matches — and someone still lost with 71
1.introduction: Gameweek 1 handed out more tiny margins and missed opportunities than sense. Paddy tops the official table with 76, Woolly thumped someone by 21, Tom managed the week's low score while sitting on nine points on the bench, and Paul scored 71 and went home gutted. All in all: predictable chaos, but fun chaos.

matches.title: Richard (Rich) 56 — Prince Majid Rd FC (Rami) 57
matches.text: Rich lost the kind of one-point scrap that makes you check your captain choice three times. Both sides leaned on Bruno for a double (four points) and João Pedro did his usual quiet 11 — but Rami's extra point was enough. Rich will now invent an injury to blame for next week.

matches.title: Humorous Name United (Rob) 72 — Roped in again (Paul) 71
matches.text: An actual thriller. Rob nicks it by one and Paul gets the modern FPL equivalent of a slap in the face: 71 and no points to show for it. Both captained the big names and both had João Pedro's 11, so this was decided by spite and marginal gains — Paul will be properly raging.

matches.title: Change Name FC (Dave) 67 — Bielsa's Babes (Paddy) 76
matches.text: Paddy went top of the official table with the week's highest score — 76 — and, despite captaining Haaland for a meagre four, still walked away with a comfortable nine-point win. Dave's 67 is nothing to sniff at, but 'Change Name FC' didn't come up with a new result to match Paddy's sheet.

matches.title: el Guapo (Tom) 47 — BeLucky Again (Kev) 51
matches.text: Tom posted the week's lowest total (47) and then remembered Granit Xhaka had nine points... on the bench. Kev shuffled his golf clubs for 51 and a neat win — Tom will insist he 'meant' to bench Xhaka, which is the same defence all of us use when we're embarrassed.

matches.title: FC Dangerous (Watson) 50 — Seattle Scorchers (Crystal) 50
matches.text: A 50-50 draw — literally. Both managers somehow produced identical scores and identical heartbreak levels. Lots of template picks and both captained Haaland into a four-point cameo; neither leaves with bragging rights, just a point each and a feeling of mild irritation.

matches.title: ChampagneSuperRovers (Dunne) 55 — Atletico Waspo (Foz) 59
matches.text: Foz's 59 edged past Dunne's 55. The usual suspects (João Pedro, a cautious defence) did the work; Dunne will complain about something being off with his midfield, Foz will sip his victory martini and remind everyone he was right about his team selection — whether they asked or not.

matches.title: Woolbrohampton (Woolly) 71 — Turf Less (Bradshaw) 50
matches.text: Woolly administered the week's biggest spanking, winning by 21. Bradshaw had Cole Palmer's 13 but it wasn't nearly enough — which is what you expect when you're a Burnley fan and someone hands you a reality check. Woolly can now spend whatever he wants and celebrate properly.

awards.text: 71 points and a loss. Paul will be replaying this one into the small hours and blaming cosmic injustice. Fair play — unlucky doesn’t cover it.
Tom scored the week's lowest total (47) and left Granit Xhaka's nine on the bench. That is criminal levels of bench placement. Xhaka would like a word.

awards.winner: Paul, Kev, Dave, Dunne, Watson, Crystal, Foz, Woolly, Tom, Bradshaw
awards.text: Everyone listed trusted Erling Haaland with the armband and got a generous four points. Congratulations on the shared misfortune — it's like buying a winning ticket for a scratchcard that says 'better luck next week'.
Biggest margin of the week: 21. Woolly turned up, spent money (probably), and left Bradshaw asking how it all went wrong. Proper textbook thump.

1.table_commentary: Using the official Super 8s ordering (H2H points, then total FPL points), Paddy sits top with Bielsa's Babes on 76. Rob (Humorous Name United) is second with 72 and Woolly is third on 71 — tidy clustering at the top. Foz and Rami occupy the next slots, while Kev's BeLucky Again sneaks into the top half. Mid-table is tight thanks to that 50-50 draw, and at the bottom Bradshaw and Tom are nursing bruises after low scores. It’s early, but plenty to complain about already.

preview.fixture: Prince Majid Rd FC (Rami) vs Woolbrohampton (Woolly)
preview.text: Rami scraped past Rich by a single point this week while Woolly put 71 on the board. This looks like a revenge/greed match: Rami will try to nick another narrow win, but Woolly's form (and willingness to spend) suggests he won't be coming quietly.

preview.fixture: Bielsa's Babes (Paddy) vs Humorous Name United (Rob)
preview.text: Paddy 76 v Rob 72 was the weekend's stand-out clash — now they meet head-to-head. Expect another high-scoring tussle and bitter post-match chat. Whoever loses will have very little dignity left.

Bradshaw got flattened 21 by Woolly and will be desperate to prove it was an anomaly; Dunne was decent but short of points. This is a chance for Bradshaw to stop the rot — or to provide more comic fodder for the rest of us.

1.closing: Week 1 delivered the usual mix of narrow margins, captaincy regrets and bench-induced shame. Keep your transfers tasteful, your captains guesswork-free and your group chat full of excuses — we'll need them next week.
